# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** — Loop through cells with black/white circle constraints on turning/straight behavior
- **Slitherlink** — Loop along grid edges with numeric constraints on surrounding line segments
- **Mid-loop** — Loop through cells where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** — Directed loop with wind constraints affecting movement direction
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop through rooms alternating between moon and sun symbols
- **Suraromu** — Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop through cells with white circles (all straight or all turning per region); avoids black circles

#### A2. Loop with Cell Shading
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoiding black cells; arrow-number clues indicate black cell counts in a direction

### B. Path/Connection Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws paths connecting specific points (not necessarily loops).

- **Numberlink** — Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect island-nodes with bridges (1 or 2 per pair); all islands connected; bridges don't cross
- **Pencils** — Draw lines from pencil tips through cells; pencil length and line length governed by numbers

### C. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver colors or paints certain cells black (or leaves them white).

#### C1. Shading with Number Clues (counting adjacent/nearby black cells)
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; all cells illuminated; no bulb-to-bulb visibility
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; circled numbers indicate sum of contiguous black cell groups extending from the circle
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells; numbers indicate count of visible white cells in four directions to nearest black cell or edge
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells to form a connected wall; numbered white islands of specified size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; numbers indicate adjacent black cell count, but exactly one number per bold-lined room is wrong

#### C2. Shading with Regional Constraints
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells in rooms; room numbers specify black cell count; no horizontal/vertical white runs spanning 3+ rooms; black cells not adjacent; white cells connected
- **Norinori** — Shade exactly two cells per bold-lined region; shaded cells form dominoes (pairs of adjacent cells)
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells; circled cells must be white "promontories" (exactly one white neighbor); numbered circles specify length of white line; no 2×2 same-color blocks
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade entire rooms to create a maze from S to G; circle rooms on shortest path; triangle rooms not on shortest path; no 2×2 same-color blocks
- **Nuritwin** — Shade cells; each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected; no 2×2 shading; blocks in same region don't touch
- **LITS** — Shade a tetromino in each bold-lined region; same-shape tetrominoes don't share edges; all shading connected; no 2×2 shading
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per number constraints; black cells don't connect across rooms; when "dropped" by gravity, stones fill the bottom half exactly

#### C3. Shading with Geometric Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Shade cells; black groups must form rectangles/squares; white groups must NOT form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles in white cells; remaining white space must form rectangles/squares; numbers on black cells count adjacent triangles

#### C4. Shading by Elimination (given numbers, remove duplicates)
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells not adjacent; white cells connected

### D. Grid Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### D1. Division into Rectangles
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area

#### D2. Division into Polyomino Regions
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate how many block boundary edges surround that cell
- **Double Choco** — Divide grid into blocks, each containing matching-shape white and gray sub-regions; numbers indicate half-block size
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends pointing toward bends; numbers indicate block size

#### D3. Division with Number Filling
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbers and divide into blocks; each block's cells all contain the same number equal to block size; same-sized blocks don't share edges
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with consecutive numbers 1 to room-size; arrow cells point to the neighbor with the largest value; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with consecutive numbers 1 to room-size; if a number N appears twice in a row/column, the gap between them must be ≥ N

### E. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver places numbers or symbols into cells.

#### E1. Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each cell; no repeats in any row, column, or 3×3 box

#### E2. Number Filling from Word Lists
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank cells with digits from a given list of multi-digit numbers, crossword-style

#### E3. Symbol Placement (non-numeric)
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference in counts; no more than 2 consecutive | horizontally or 2 consecutive — vertically (and analogous 3+ rules)

### F. Object Placement/Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves objects within the grid.

#### F1. Placement of Objects
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes can't touch; line-of-sight attack constraint from head direction
- **Evolomino** — Place squares to form blocks along arrows; each successive block on an arrow's path adds one cell to the previous block's shape without rotation/flip

#### F2. Movement of Objects
- **Satogaeri** — Move numbered circles within bold-lined countries so each country has exactly one; numbers specify distance moved; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move all circles straight into gray areas; arrows don't cross each other or other circles; gray area numbers equal sum of entering circle values

### G. Hybrid: Shading + Connectivity with Specialized Constraints
- **Chained Block** — Shade cells to form "blocks" (connected groups); each block has one number/? indicating its size; all blocks must be part of a "chain" (corner-touching group); no duplicate size+shape within a chain
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire bold-lined tiles; diagonal-cell numbers specify black cell counts in the row/column segment to the right or below

---

## II. Cross-Cutting Structural Properties

### By Connectivity Constraints on Shaded Cells
| Constraint | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| All black cells connected | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin |
| All white cells connected | Hitori, Kurodoko, Heyawake, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Nurimeizu |
| Both black and white connected | (implied in several) |
| No 2×2 black square | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu |
| No 2×2 same-color square | Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu |
| Black cells not orthogonally adjacent | Hitori, Heyawake, Usowan, Yajilin, Kurodoko |

### By Use of Bold-Lined Rooms/Regions
- **With rooms:** Heyawake, Norinori, LITS, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Fillomino (implicit), Moon-or-Sun, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Five Cells, Usowan, Dotchi-Loop, Choco Banana, Sto-stone, Sashigane, Satogaeri, Suraromu, Tilepaint, Hebi
- **Without rooms:** Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Numberlink, Hashiwokakero, Hitori, Sudoku, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Akari, Nurikabe, Yajilin, Nagareru, Nansuke, Yosenabe, Pencils

### By Clue Type
| Clue Type | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| Numbers count adjacent features | Akari, Slitherlink, Five Cells, Shakashaka, Usowan, Kurotto |
| Numbers indicate region/block size | Shikaku, Fillomino, Choco Banana, Sashigane, Double Choco, Chained Block, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, LITS (implicit=4), Five Cells (implicit=5) |
| Numbers indicate visible/reachable cells | Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Akari (implicit illumination) |
| Numbers indicate room fill count | Heyawake, Sto-stone, Makaro, Ripple Effect |
| Arrows indicate direction | Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Nagareru, Sashigane, Evolomino, Yosenabe, Pencils |
| Numbers on objects indicate movement distance | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| Ordered/sequential constraints | Suraromu (gate ordering), Hebi (1–5 sequence), Pencils (line length), Evolomino (progressive growth) |
